title: Invertibility of the ordinary open quotient mate
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l, and an OrdinaryLimitModel a [def-sf-integral-system-canonical-bridge]. For any open immersion j:X→Y, an ordinary system extension o left adjoint to the specified system inverse image [def-sf-integral-system-operations], and any completed-coefficient module M on X, the component at M of the inverse open-adjunction mate of a.reductionPull is an isomorphism of ordinary coherent coefficient systems. The assertion is before passage to complexes and derived localization and has no completeness hypothesis.

source.place: Maps-used sentence, open-factor normalization: the ordinary section-normalized quotient/open map.

proof.text: The integral open extension is fully faithful: present it as an equivalence followed by extension on the slice of a subterminal open. Its adjunction unit at M is therefore invertible.

The finite quotient of integral open extension lies in the finite open essential image. Apply the finite evaluation counit square to the ordinary reduction of that extension. Reduction evaluation identifies each component with this quotient, so each evaluated system counit is invertible. Evaluation jointly reflects isomorphisms by forgetting to sectionwise abelian groups on the sequence site.

Expand the actual inverse adjunction mate: it is system extension of reduction applied to the integral open unit, followed by system extension of the isomorphism a.reductionPull, then the system counit at the reduced extended object. All factors are invertible, so their composite is invertible. No change to the specified mate or its statement is made.
